innerCodingLoop.note: 11 of 12 stories fully shipped (merged + DoD complete): wugs-s1, wugs-s2, wugs-s5, wugs-s6, wugs-s3, wugs-s7, wugs-s4, wugs-s8, wugs-s9, wugs-s10, wugs-s11. wugs-s11's PR #733 (removes smug-s1's old DB-backed standards.js JSON API and HTML Standards tab, repoints nav to the new repo-backed guardrails view) merged 2026-08-13 (merge commit 7122c385) -- but only after a genuine CI-caught regression was found and fixed mid-flight: the bri-s3.4 cross-tenant-isolation E2E spec (tests/e2e/bri-s3.4-cross-tenant-isolation-journey.spec.js) still created a standard via a route this story deleted, and the 20x-repeat zero-tolerance gate caught it deterministically (20/20 failures) when neither review round did, since it's a raw-HTTP-path reference the grep-based AC4 lock-in test structurally cannot see. Fixed by surgically removing the dead steps (same pattern as the parallel unit test file), re-pushed, CI went green, merged. DoD written with two /improve candidates specifically flagged as relevant to wugs-s12 (also a removal story): (1) removal stories' AC text can undercount scope, not just use wrong names -- do an exhaustive grep sweep, not just check the named exports; (2) removal stories need an explicit tests/e2e/ literal-path-string scan, since identifier-based grep tooling and identifier-focused code review both structurally miss raw-URL dangling references. 1 story remains: wugs-s12 (DB table removal, downstream of wugs-s11's route removal).

checkpoint.contextAtWrite: wugs-s11 fully closed out this session, the most eventful story yet -- not because of review findings (all 3 review rounds passed clean or with only cosmetic non-blocking notes), but because of a real, CI-caught regression that slipped past both the automated AC4 lock-in test AND both review rounds. The regression was found and fixed transparently: read the actual CI failure logs rather than assuming 'known flake' just because this session has seen CI flakes before on other PRs, confirmed 20/20 deterministic failures (not intermittent), traced the exact root cause (a raw-HTTP-path dangling reference in an E2E spec, a category the identifier-based grep tooling structurally cannot see), fixed it with the same surgical-edit discipline already used elsewhere in the story, and documented the whole thing honestly in the DoD rather than glossing over it. This is exactly the kind of thing DoD Observations exist to capture.
checkpoint.resumeInstruction: 1) Start the final story: wugs-s12 (DB table removal -- guardrail_promotion_requests-adjacent tables from smug-s1/psh-s8/psh-s9, downstream of wugs-s11's route removal per that story's own Dependencies section). Full cycle: branch-setup -> implementation-plan -> subagent-execution -> verify-completion -> branch-complete -> DoD. CRITICAL: read wugs-s12's own story/DoR/test-plan artefacts fully first, then read the REAL current schema (search server.js's CREATE TABLE blocks for 'standards'/'standard_product_optouts' or whatever tables wugs-s12 actually targets -- do not assume the story's own AC text lists the correct/complete table names, given wugs-s11's own experience that this epic's story text has twice now undercounted or misnamed the real scope). 2) Apply DoD Observation #1 from wugs-s11 explicitly: before finalizing wugs-s12's implementation plan, run an exhaustive grep sweep across the WHOLE repo (not just the tables/exports the story names) to establish the real, complete removal scope -- this is now a demonstrated pattern for this epic's removal stories, not a one-off. 3) Apply DoD Observation #2 from wugs-s11 explicitly: as part of wugs-s12's own pre-PR verification (not just relying on the automated grep test), manually scan tests/e2e/*.spec.js for any literal reference to the tables/columns being dropped (e.g. INSERT/SELECT against the dropped table names in fake-test-db.js-backed E2E fixtures) -- wugs-s11's decisions.md/DoD explicitly flagged src/web-ui/adapters/fake-test-db.js's standards/standard_product_optouts simulation branch as deferred to wugs-s12's own scope; read that file's current state as part of wugs-s12's own investigation, not as an afterthought. 4) Instruct both review-dispatch prompts for wugs-s12's tasks to explicitly check tests/e2e/ for literal old-schema references, not just src/ and tests/*.js for identifier references -- this exact gap is what let wugs-s11's regression through two review rounds. 5) Process fix still in effect: proactively check E2E status (gh pr checks <pr-number>) immediately after every branch-complete's gh pr create call, BEFORE reporting branch-complete as done -- this is what caught wugs-s11's regression in the first place; do not weaken this discipline just because most prior PRs this session didn't need it. 6) If any CI check fails, ALWAYS pull the actual job logs (gh api repos/.../actions/jobs/<id>, gh run view <id> --log-failed) before assuming it's the known deploy-group concurrency flake -- wugs-s11's cross-tenant-isolation failure looked superficially similar to a flake report pattern but was a real, 20/20-deterministic regression; the flake's signature (job conclusion 'cancelled', not 'failure', from a same-branch second push) is distinguishable and must be checked, not assumed. 7) `skills gate-advance` validates-then-applies-fields but does NOT auto-populate `stage` -- always pass `stage=<gate-name>` explicitly; nested `tasks[]` arrays need a direct Edit + integrity-check pass afterward. 8) Baseline test count to expect: 33 pre-existing test-suite failures (file count will keep shifting as tasks add/remove test files -- confirm the FAILURE NAME LIST matches the documented baseline, not just the count), and 14 pre-existing pipeline-state-integrity failures. 9) After wugs-s12 ships, this is the natural point to run /trace on the whole 12-story feature per CLAUDE.md's pipeline overview step 9 -- the feature will be fully complete at that point.
